title: abusekit label-snapshot corpus row (corpus-v2)
description: One line of a label-snapshot corpus JSONL file (design docs/design/2026-09-27-abusekit-design.md §4.6/§4.9, and docs/plans/2026-09-27-v0-plan.md's S4 row). This is the PUBLISHED schema `abusekit eval --dataset ...` and `abusekit corpus export --schema corpus-v2.json` both speak. eval/dataset.go's LoadSnapshotCorpus enforces this schema in Go directly (no JSON-Schema validation library is a dependency of this module — see AGENTS.md's 'keep the dependency footprint minimal'); this file is the published, human- and tool-readable contract that Go code is written to match, not something re-parsed at runtime.

id.description: Unique row identifier. Duplicate ids within one corpus file are a schema violation.

features.description: The full named feature vector as internal/feature.Features.Map() produces it (design §4.5), keyed by feature name (e.g. "core.subject_age_h"). A rule's own `inputs:` list selects a subset at score time — this row is not rule-specific.

text.description: Text-bearing field values, keyed by field name (e.g. "subject_line_skeleton", "first_link_host" — internal/event's redaction schema's skeleton-companion fields). A rule's own `text:` list selects a subset. Each value is an ORDERED list because a subject can have emitted the same text-bearing event type more than once (e.g. several content.sent events, each contributing one subject_line_skeleton).

context.description: Free-form context a renderer may prepend (model.ScoreRequest.Context).

input.description: input.features and input.text must not BOTH be empty/absent — a row with neither has nothing for any rule to score.

label.description: Ground-truth label, in whichever vocabulary the row's rule/subject uses (design §4.9: a rule's own `labels:` list, or the fixed subject-level benign|abusive pair). eval's metrics treat any value other than the scored rule's `benign_label` as the positive (abusive) class.

split.description: design §4.9: "split by link cluster (fallback subject) hashed 80/20". Omitted or empty means the row has no assigned split; `abusekit eval --dataset ...` scores every row regardless of split unless a future flag filters on it.

source.description: Label provenance (design §4.9: "operator"|"outcome", matching a labels-file row's own `source`).

meta.description: Free-form metadata carried through to Verdict/run.json for a human reading the run; never consulted by scoring.
